correctness.rationale: For each preferred-color occupancy \(k\), the local triangle cost satisfies \(f(r)\ge 1-r\), \(f(r)\ge r-1\), and \(f(r)\ge 2r-3\), giving the global lower bound \(\max\{10-2k,2k-10,4k-30\}\). The Petersen graph has no proper three-edge-coloring because the complement of each perfect matching comprises two odd five-cycles; incidence parity additionally forbids a single defective vertex, raising the only exceptional \(k=5\) bound to two. Sixteen explicit 15-edge color strings attain every sector lower bound. Two dissimilar complete algorithms independently count all \(3^{15}=14{,}348{,}907\) configurations and obtain identical occupancy-sector minima and multiplicities. The exact five-line field envelope and coexistence counts follow by affine minimization.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is the smallest snark and a canonical minimal obstruction to three-edge-coloring. Its line-graph 3-state Potts model is the natural physical penalty relaxation of this obstruction. The computed ground states have a four-to-six preferred-color occupancy jump across an arbitrarily small zero-field bias, a phenomenon absent from defect-free three-edge-colorings of class-I cubic graphs. The full exact ground-energy envelope, four coexistence multiplicities, and 1800-state zero-field classification are nontrivial and reusable finite-cluster benchmarks, not arbitrary parameter slicing or a bulk-phase claim.
